FIELD REFERENCE

Bull trout (Salvelinus confluentus): size, range, ID

The bull trout is Salvelinus confluentus, a char native to the Pacific Northwest, Alaska and Canada. It is olive in colour with pale orange, round spots on its sides. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service gives a common length of 25 inches. It needs cold, clean, complex and connected water, mostly deep pools of large, cold rivers and lakes.

Updated 2026-11-21 · Castward

What is a bull trout?

Key factDetail
Scientific nameSalvelinus confluentus; a char
Other namesBull char; omble à tête plate in Canadian French (FishBase)
How to identify itOlive or drab body with pale orange, round spots along the sides
SizeCommon length 25 inches; maximum reported 40.5 inches and 31 pounds 15 ounces (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service)
RangeNorthwestern North America from Alaska to northern California. FishBase lists Arctic, Pacific and Missouri River drainages from southern Yukon to northern Nevada and the McCloud River drainage
HabitatDeep pools of large, cold rivers and lakes; most common in high mountain areas with snowfields and glaciers
The Four CsCold, clean, complex and connected habitat
SpawningUsually August to November, in small streams over clean gravel. Females lay about 5,000 eggs on average, and the eggs stay in the gravel for up to 210 days
MaturityUsually at four to seven years; a fish may spawn each year or every second year

What should you know about bull trout?

Is a bull trout a trout or a char?

It is a char. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service describes bull trout as a char native to the Pacific Northwest, Alaska and Canada. Its genus, Salvelinus, is the char genus.

How big do bull trout get?

The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service gives a common length of 25 inches, a maximum reported length of 40.5 inches and a maximum reported weight of 31 pounds 15 ounces.

Where do bull trout live?

In northwestern North America, from Alaska to northern California, in mountain and coastal streams. They are most common in high mountain areas and stay mainly in deep pools of large, cold rivers and lakes.

What are the Four Cs of bull trout habitat?

Cold, clean, complex and connected. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service uses these four words for the water that bull trout need.

Do bull trout migrate?

Most do. Some stay in one stream for life, but most move to larger rivers or lakes to feed and spend the winter, then return to small streams to spawn. A rare form goes to the sea.

When do bull trout spawn?

Typically between August and November, and sometimes as late as December. Females dig nests, called redds, in clean gravel.

Can you fish for bull trout?

It depends on the water. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service lists habitat damage, dams and non-native fish as pressures on bull trout, and rules can prohibit harvest. Read the rules of the state or provincial fisheries agency for the exact water and date before you fish.
